$comment: ZoFHub — DEFAULT sing-box profile: local egress for the proxy browser.
This is the profile ZoFHub runs out of the box. sing-box listens on a
LOOPBACK-ONLY SOCKS5/HTTP inbound, and every TCP stream the Wisp tunnel
opens for a visitor is dialled through it (lib/singbox-socket.mjs). That is
what puts sing-box in the site's real traffic path rather than beside it.
WHY THIS PROFILE AND NOT THE REALITY ONE. A VLESS+REALITY inbound has to
own :443 to borrow a real site's TLS handshake, which the platform edge
already owns on a normal single-container deploy — so it cannot be the
default. It is still shipped, as config.reality.template.json, for hosts
where you control the network edge. See docs/proxy/SINGBOX.md.
NO SECRETS ARE REQUIRED. The management API secret is generated at boot if
SINGBOX_API_SECRET is unset, so the default deploy needs no configuration.
Validate after editing:  sing-box check -c config.json
Written against the sing-box 1.11+ schema (route rule `action`, not the
removed `block` outbound). The supervisor runs `check` before every start,
so a schema mismatch surfaces as one error line, never a crash loop.
The Clash-compatible management API — the ONE surface ZoFHub reads
(lib/singbox.mjs → GET /api/admin/proxy).
LOOPBACK ONLY, ALWAYS. Anyone who reaches this API can rewrite routing
and enumerate every live connection. ZoFHub reads it server-side
precisely so no browser ever touches it.
`mixed` speaks SOCKS5 and HTTP CONNECT on one port. ZoFHub uses SOCKS5.
Note that the CONNECT usually carries an IP, not a name: ZoFHub resolves
and validates the destination itself before dialling (rebinding
protection), so this daemon is the egress hop, not the resolver.
listen is 127.0.0.1 and must stay that way on a shared host: an open
SOCKS proxy on a public interface is an abuse relay within hours.
Rules match in order; `final` is the fallback.
The private/loopback reject is load-bearing, not decorative. Without it a
proxied visitor could ask sing-box for 127.0.0.1 — which includes the
clash_api controller above, the ZoFHub web server itself, and on a cloud
host the 169.254.169.254 instance-metadata endpoint that hands out
credentials. wisp-js applies its own SSRF filter before the stream is
opened; this is the second, independent layer, and neither trusts the
other to be correct.
`action: reject` replaces the `block` outbound type removed after 1.11.
